summary: Lower a non-constructable use of an anonymous function expression to a C# delegate when JS function-object metadata is unobserved.

target.notes: This is a specialization: ordinary function expressions are constructable in JS, so delegate lowering is only valid when construction/prototype identity cannot be observed.

semantics.constructability: ignored only because analysis proves new/prototype are unobservable

caveats: Do not use this rule if identity, prototype, name/length descriptors, caller/arguments, or construction are observable.

tests.name: simple callback
tests.input: const inc = function(x){ return x + 1; }; console.log(inc(2));

tests.name: fresh identity must remain fresh
tests.input: function make(){ return function(x){return x}; } console.log(make() === make());
tests.expected_behavior: prints false; compiler must allocate distinct delegate objects or otherwise preserve identity
